title: The verb 'to be' (ni)
description: The copula 'ni' links a subject to a noun or adjective and does not change for person.

title: The verb 'to have' (kuwa na)
description: Swahili has no verb 'have'; it uses 'kuwa na' (to be with), shown by the -na- tense prefix.

title: Personal pronouns
description: Independent subject pronouns in Swahili.

title: Days of the week
description: Swahili days of the week all begin with 'Juma' or 'Iju'.

title: Months of the year
description: Swahili month names, mostly borrowed from other languages.

title: Numbers 0–20
description: Basic cardinal numbers; 11–19 are formed with 'kumi na' (ten and).

title: The -na- present tense
description: The -na- infix marks an action happening now, made from subject prefix + na + verb.

title: Question words
description: Common Swahili question words used to ask about people, things, time and place.

title: Demonstratives (this / that)
description: Swahili has no articles; demonstratives agree with the noun class.

title: Locatives -ni / kwa / katika
description: Place is expressed with the suffix -ni or with locative words like juu ya and chini ya.

title: Past tense of 'to be' (kuwa)
description: The past of kuwa uses -li- with the subject prefix plus irregular negative forms.

title: Comparatives and superlatives (kuliko, zaidi ya)
description: Comparison is built with kuliko or zaidi ya, and the superlative adds wote.
rows: grande / más grande / el más grande
pequeño / más pequeño / el más pequeño
alto / más alto / el más alto
bajo / más bajo / el más bajo

title: The present continuous with -na-
description: The -na- tense marks actions happening now, with a subject prefix on every verb.

title: Common verbs in the past tense (-li-)
description: High-frequency verbs form the past with the -li- infix and a subject prefix.

title: The future tense -ta-
description: The -ta- tense for predictions, decisions, promises and future plans.
rows: We are going to travel tomorrow.
Look, it is going to rain.

title: The perfect tense -me-
description: The -me- tense for actions completed with present relevance.

title: The passive with the suffix -wa
description: Forming passives with the verb extension -wa and its allomorphs.
rows: They read the book; the book is read.
They are building a house; a house is being built.
Someone stole the car; the car was stolen.
The company signed the contract; the contract was signed.

title: Connectors and linking words
description: Conjunctions and connectors for complex sentences.

title: Noun class plurals
description: Swahili nouns fall into classes; the plural is shown by the noun's prefix.

title: Possessive stems (-angu, -ako, -ake)
description: Possessives agree with the noun class and follow the noun.

title: Demonstratives (this / that)
description: Swahili demonstratives change with noun class and distance.

title: There is / there are: kuna / hakuna
description: Kuna introduces existence and hakuna negates it, regardless of number.
rows: There is a book on the table.
Hay un libro en la mesa.
There are two books on the table.
Hay dos libros en la mesa.

title: Past continuous (nilikuwa + -na-)
description: Combine the past of kuwa with the -na- form to describe an action in progress in the past.

title: Quantifiers: -ingi, -chache, kidogo
description: Express amount with agreeing quantifiers and words like kidogo and kadhaa.

title: The first conditional with -ki-
description: A real future condition uses the -ki- tense in the if-clause and a future tense in the result.
rows: If I study, I will pass.
If he comes, I will tell him.
If we leave now, we will arrive on time.
Si salimos ahora, llegaremos a tiempo.
If it rains, I will stay at home.
Si llueve, me quedaré en casa.
If you call, I will answer you.

title: Reported speech (kwamba)
description: Statements are reported with kwamba, often keeping the original tense.

title: Relative clauses and the relative infix
description: Relative clauses with the infix -ye-/-o-/-lo-, amba- and agreement.
rows: Mtu aliyepiga simu ni bosi wangu.
The man who called is my boss.
El hombre que llamó es mi jefe.
The book which you lent me was great.
El libro que me prestaste era genial.
Kaka yangu, ambaye anaishi Roma, ni daktari.
My brother, who lives in Rome, is a doctor.
Mi hermano, que vive en Roma, es médico.
Mwanamke ambaye gari lake liliibwa alipiga polisi.
The woman whose car was stolen called the police.
La mujer cuyo coche fue robado llamó a la policía.
That is the house where I grew up.
Esa es la casa donde crecí.

title: Unreal past with -ngali-/-nge-
description: Counterfactual past conditions with kama plus the -ngali- verb form.
rows: If I had studied, I would have passed.
If we had left earlier, we would not have missed the train.
Si hubiéramos salido antes, no habríamos perdido el tren.
If she had known, she would have come.
Si ella lo hubiera sabido, habría venido.
If they had invested, they would have made a profit.
Si hubieran invertido, habrían obtenido beneficios.

title: Counting and mass nouns
description: Some Swahili nouns are counted directly, others use quantity words.

title: Imperatives (amri)
description: Commands use the verb stem; the negative uses 'usi-' and the plural adds '-ni'.

title: Time expressions (in / on / at)
description: Swahili marks time with dates, 'mwezi wa' and 'mwaka'.

title: Possessive pronouns (-angu, -ako, -ake)
description: Possessive stems take the prefix of the noun they agree with.

title: Adverbs of frequency
description: Adverbs such as kila mara and mara nyingi show how often something happens.
rows: Yeye kwa kawaida huenda kazini kwa miguu.
Sisi mara nyingi tunawatembelea babu na bibi.
A menudo visitamos a nuestros abuelos.
Yeye wakati mwingine husahau funguo zake.

title: Future tense (-ta-)
description: The -ta- infix marks actions that will happen in the future.

title: The hypothetical -nge- conditional
description: An unreal or hypothetical condition uses -nge- in both the condition and the result.
rows: Si ganara la lotería, viajaría por el mundo.
Si tuviera más tiempo, aprendería a tocar la guitarra.
Si ella estuviera aquí, nos ayudaría.
Si viviéramos junto al mar, nadaríamos todos los días.

title: Obligation: lazima, inabidi, -paswa
description: Obligation and advice are expressed with lazima, inabidi and the verb -paswa.

title: Fronting and negative emphasis
description: Emphatic fronting and negative-concord structures in formal Swahili.
rows: No sooner had I arrived than it rained.
Hii ni nafuu na pia nzuri.
Si nafuu tu, bali pia nzuri.
This is not only cheap but also good.
No solo es barato, sino también bueno.

title: Reduced clauses with the situative -ki-
description: Compressing clauses with the situative -ki- and the ku- infinitive.
rows: Kwa sababu alikuwa amechoka, alikwenda kulala.
Because she was tired, she went to bed.
Como estaba cansada, se fue a la cama.
When he arrived, he called us.
The book, written in 1990, is famous.
El libro, escrito en 1990, es famoso.
Kwa kuwa nilikuwa nimemaliza kazi, nilikwenda nyumbani.
Since I had finished work, I went home.
Habiendo terminado el trabajo, me fui a casa.

title: There was / there were (kulikuwa na)
description: Past form of 'kuna', using 'kulikuwa na' for both singular and plural.

title: Liking verbs + infinitive (ku-)
description: Verbs like -penda, -chukia and -furahia take an infinitive with 'ku-'.

title: Possession with -a (gari la John)
description: Swahili shows possession with the connective '-a' agreeing with the noun.
rows: El coche de John es rojo.

title: Past tense (-li-)
description: The -li- infix marks completed actions in the past.

title: Reflexive infix -ji-
description: The infix -ji- shows the action falls back on the subject.

title: Question tags (sivyo? / sawa?)
description: Short tags like sivyo? and sawa? are added at the end of a statement.
rows: She doesn't like coffee, does she?

title: Passive with modals (-w-)
description: The passive extension -w- combines with modals to say what must or can be done.
rows: Las entradas pueden comprarse en línea.

title: Wishes and regrets (laiti, -ngali-)
description: Wishes and regrets use laiti with -nge- for the present and -ngali- for the past.
rows: I wish I had more time.
I wish it would stop raining.

title: Cleft and focus constructions
description: Focusing one part of a sentence with ni ... and ninacho-/alicho- clefts.
rows: Maria broke the window; it was Maria who broke the window.
Fue María quien rompió la ventana.
I need a holiday; what I need is a holiday.
Lo que necesito son unas vacaciones.
He only wanted to help; all he wanted was to help.
Todo lo que quería era ayudar.

title: Hedging and academic tone
description: Cautious, formal language for essays and academic writing.
rows: Hii inaonyesha kwamba nadharia huenda ni sahihi.
This suggests the theory may be correct.
Esto sugiere que la teoría puede ser correcta.
The results appear to be inconsistent.

title: Asking quantity (ngapi / kiasi gani)
description: 'ngapi' asks 'how many', 'kiasi gani' asks 'how much'.
rows: How many apples do you want?

title: Ability and permission (-weza)
description: '-weza' with an infinitive expresses ability and permission.

title: Adverbs of manner
description: Swahili expresses how an action is done with adverbs or 'kwa' + noun.

title: Prepositions of movement
description: Verbs of movement combine with locative words and the -ni suffix.
rows: Caminaron a lo largo del río.

title: Both / neither / either
description: Words for talking about two things: -ote mbili, wala, yoyote.
rows: Ninguna de las dos respuestas es correcta.
Cualquiera de los dos días me vale.

title: Something / anything / nothing
description: Indefinite pronouns such as kitu, mtu and chochote.
rows: There is nothing in the box.
No hay nada en la caja.

title: Reported questions (kama, question words)
description: Reported questions use kama for yes/no and keep the question word for wh-questions.

title: Verb + infinitive (ku-) vs subjunctive
description: Many Swahili verbs take a following ku- infinitive as their complement.

title: The subjunctive -e
description: The subjunctive ending -e after verbs of wanting, suggesting and necessity.
rows: I suggest that he go home.
Sugiero que se vaya a casa.
It is important that he be here.

title: Discourse markers for essays
description: Connectors that organise formal and academic writing.
